expected_title: Mathematical Representation of Stakeholder Preferences for the SPORT Small Satellite Project
abstract: The design of complex systems involves mu ltiple stakeholders with various preferences working together to realize a single system . Th e interfaces existing between the subsystems creates a complex system in itself. While contributing to the same system, design teams have unique objectives to their team and the subsystem they are designing. T he preferences of individuals within each design team may also be unique , adding to the overall pro ject complexity . Differing preferences often lead to challenges in many aspects of systems engineering, such as leadership, project management, contracting and interface documentation . This paper is a first step to overcome such challenges by understanding the impac t of differing preferences on system design. The aim of the paper will be to mathematically represen t a small satellite system’s stakeholders’ preferences using value models based on general beliefs about organizational goals . Specific to this study, stakeholders represent various organizations , both in the top management level as well as design teams de veloping the subsystems for t he Scintillation Prediction Observation Research Task ( SPORT ). Four value models were created to represent the preferences of stakeholders involved in the SPORT project. The attributes affecting these differing preferences were identified, and the expected implication of these attributes on the satellite design was discussed. While the value models depict preference that were specific to each organization, similarities of p references amongst stakeholders could also be found. Fut ure work will compare the presented value models to value models generated by the stakeholders through survey research .
